**Optional.** Reference for readers who use one of these clusters. Shared
by @sec-orientation, @sec-working-remotely, and @sec-hpc-slurm.

## Planned topics

- Who can get an account, and how to apply (SCINet for USDA-affiliated
  users; ISU Nova for Iowa State users); how long approval takes
- Logging in: host names, multi-factor authentication, first login,
  published host-key fingerprints
- Data transfer nodes: Nova `novadtn.its.iastate.edu`; SCINet
  `ceres-dtn.scinet.usda.gov`, `atlas-dtn.hpc.msstate.edu`; Globus
- Storage areas, quotas, and what is backed up (home, project, scratch)
- Nova quotas (checked 2026-11-20): no quota command (`quota -s`
  prints nothing; the documented `cdw` is missing; `my_workdir`
  lower-cases the group and fails for `/work/ABG`). Home 10 GB, check
  with `du -sh ~`. Group: `cat /work/<group>/group_storage_usage`
  (group `NAME AVAIL USED`, fraction used, then per user `TYPE NAME
  USED QUOTA OBJUSED OBJQUOTA`, where OBJ counts files); `df -h
  /work/<group>` shows the same group share
- Ceres quotas (checked 2026-11-20): `my_quotas` (`/usr/local/bin`)
  lists home, each `/project/<name>`, and Juno `/LTS/project/<name>`,
  with columns `Path`, `Usage (GB)`, `Quota (GB)`, `Availible (GB)`
  (sic), `Consumed (%)`, `Status`; home about 30 GB (`quota -s` also
  works for home: `30518M` quota, `50545M` limit, no file limit);
  `/90daydata` has no quota but deletes data 90 days after last access;
  `df -h /project/<name>` shows the project's quota as the size
- Shared group folders: Nova `/work/<group>` is `drwxrws--T`, owned by
  `root` and the lab's group (setgid on, sticky, closed to others); new
  files take the lab's group and, with Nova's umask `0002`, are
  group-writable (captured 2026-11-20). Ceres `/project/<name>` is also
  `drwxrws--T` (`root`, group `proj-<name>`); new files take
  `proj-<name>` but, with SCINet's umask `0027`, are `-rw-r-----`
  (group reads, cannot edit); your primary group is a personal one
  (captured 2026-11-20)
- Ceres vs Atlas: one comparison table (login, DTN, and OnDemand hosts;
  separate storage and quotas for the same projects; OnDemand apps;
  hardware and partitions; location), checked against SCINet's pages
- Software on the site: modules, containers, and where pixi fits
- VS Code on each site: the supported route (Nova: VS Code Tunnel app or
  VS Code Server in Open OnDemand, Remote-SSH only to compute nodes;
  SCINet: VS Code Server in Open OnDemand or a registered tunnel to Ceres
  compute nodes), what each needs (VPN; Microsoft or GitHub account),
  ending a session to release its resources, and moving the code-server
  folder from `$HOME` to project storage
- Sources: [ISU: Using VS Code on the cluster](https://research.it.iastate.edu/using-vs-code-cluster),
  [SCINet: VS Code guide](https://scinet.usda.gov/guides/ide/vscode)
- Where to get help: each site's own documentation and support contacts
